messages:
omar: Heads-up — saw weird oscillation in prefix-KV hit rate after last deploy + autoscale. Hit-rate jumps to ~90% then collapses to single digits within ~3m after scale-out. Anyone seen this pattern?
jen: yeah seen that before with per-replica caches. new replicas join empty so overall global hit-rate drops while autoscaler spins up.
micah: can you paste the metric? what labels (model/route/replica) are we using?
omar: snippet from grafana (simplified):
```
time       global_hit_rate pct
10:03:00   92
10:04:10   87
10:05:00   11  <-- autoscale from 8->32
10:06:00    9
10:10:00   14
```
Labels: model=redwood-v1, route=chat-standard, replica=shard-*-*
liam: interesting — autoscale multiplier looks high. are warmers running on new machines?
omar: we had deploy-time warmers enabled, but they run as a Job that targets old replicas only (bug?). ops-bot reported: `Job finished with 0 targets matched`
rachel: Ah ok. this matches an earlier config where the prefill job selector used deployment label `app: has-warmers=true` and new instances have `app: runtime-v2` during scaling.
micah: two vectors to fix: 1) make warmers target by service name (stable) or by scheduler that waits for new replica readiness; 2) avoid thundering-herd when many replicas prefill simultaneously.
jen: we experimented with a lease-based prefill coordinator last quarter: coordinator grants N leases per model to limit concurrency, prefill runs until lease expires. reduced CPU spike and cache churn.
omar: example config we had:
```
# scheduler: k8s cronjob wrapper
prefill_controller:
  max_concurrent_leases: 3
  lease_ttl: 60s
  splay_window: 30s
  diversity_sample: [short, medium, long]
```
liam: also saw perf regressions when warm traffic only used short prompts — kernel selection favored small-kernel path and when real traffic with long sequences hit, the runtime picked different kernels causing microcode thrash. include distribution of lengths in warmers.
jen: +1. our dogfood run that matched prod seq-length histogram improved p95 stability.
micah: another trick — seed prefix shard keys deterministically so new replicas can request a small subset of hot prefixes first (head-of-hotlist). example: for each model route, precompute top-100 prefixes and round-robin them across replicas during prefill.
omar: we tried that briefly. result: global hit-rate recovered from 12% -> 78% within 7m and p50 token latency unchanged. p95 improved by ~150ms.
perf-bot: metric-report: prefill-change-2026-03-10 -> hit_rate: 12% -> 78% in 7m; p95 latency delta: -150ms; cpu spike: +18% briefly during prefill; error rate: no change.
rachel: Nice. We should add two safety knobs: (A) max-prefill-qps per-replica, (B) backoff on cache-eviction pressure. If eviction rate > threshold, slow warmers.
liam: for autoscale events, we should also try a hybrid model: light-weight prefix fingerprinting (not full KV load) at startup to prime kernel selection and batching heuristics, followed by heavier KV prefill for top prefixes. fingerprinting is cheap: run 1 token forward with cached kv meta to choose kernel path.
omar: code snippet for cheap fingerprinting probe:
```
for r in new_replicas:
  curl -X POST $r/internal/fingerprint -d '{"sample_prefixes": 5, "probe_len": 8}'
```
If fingerprint indicates long-seq path, mark replica as "warm-for-long" and schedule corresponding prefill set.
jen: ops-suggestion: stagger replica readiness with a splay formula to avoid simultaneous prefill storms. e.g., splay = random(0, min(60s, scale_delta * 5s)).
micah: also add telemetry: per-replica prefix-hit histogram and prefill-success events. we need to know which prefixes moved hit-rate.
omar: action items: 1) fix selector for deploy warmers to target service name (jen) 2) enable lease-based prefill coordinator (micah + ops) 3) add sequence-length diversity to warmers (liam) 4) implement cheap fingerprint probe (omar) 5) add eviction backoff + per-replica QPS cap (rachel). I can roll a small run tomorrow.
jen: I'll open a PR for selector fix and small unit test.
micah: I'll spin up coordinator proto and test on staging with scale 2->12. expect metrics by EOD.
ops-bot: scheduled job created: staging-prefill-test-2026-03-11 09:00 UTC :eyes:
omar: thanks — if staging looks good we'll stage to canary with splay 30s then prod. :thumbsup:
